subject: How can I limit chart disable/fading on processing?

messages.author: 782ed6ec348dba9b
messages.subject: How can I limit chart disable/fading on processing?
parts:
When there is a user interaction which is intended to result in a changed chart, the chart fades presumably to indicate
to the user that there is some processing underway

I am trying to develop an app which polls a website every minute (for  an updated sports score) and potentially does some quite intensive processing on the results returned

 data <- reactive({

   invalidateLater(60000, session)

## poll url and produce a character vector 'results'

# process 'results' with end-product info including data.frame, df

return(info)
})

output$chart <- renderPlot({
# process data()$df  to produce chart
})

Currently, the processing of all the results takes about a minute so the chart gets redrawn and immediately fades away for re-processing
I would ideally like to limit the processing to take place only if length(results) differs between consecutive polls and then just add rows as necessary
to df. This would significantly reduce the time the chart is in processing-mode but I am not sure how to store and use the previous' results' and 'df'

Alternatively, is there a way to turn off the fading so that the chart remains fully visible other when redrawing is necessary?

cheers

Thanks for that. Did not quite fathom it out so if anyone does a gist on it for my type of requirement, please post here

I think I have solved problem by saving the initial download as a csv file then reading it again
when I have rescraped the website and compare lengths. If there is no difference, I just make the original
calculated data (which I also saved) available again to my chart. Otherwise I carry on in the reactive just processing  the new data,
combine it with the old processed and reissue to renderChart
